title: Microsoft Purview Content Explorer: enhanced filter for sensitive information types and labels (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing and Content Explorer access controls are supported. It correctly distinguishes documented explorer functionality from the still-unspecified details of the enhanced filter.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap introduces enhanced Content Explorer UI controls for scoped visibility and filtering of SIT and label data.
claims.quote: Introduces enhanced controls in Content Explorer’s UI, enabling scoped visibility and filtering of SIT and label data. This will help with content discoverability and governance.

claims.claim: Content Explorer is accessed in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Explorers > Content explorer.

claims.quote: You can create customized views in content explorer, by configuring what SITs, Sensitivity Labels, Trainable Classifiers, and Retention Labels which are important for you.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Microsoft highly restricts Content Explorer access because it permits reading scanned-file contents.
claims.quote: Access to content explorer is highly restricted because it lets you read the contents of scanned files.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Content Explorer viewing permissions supersede permissions locally assigned to items.
claims.quote: These permissions supersede permissions that are locally assigned to the items, which allow viewing of the content.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Content Explorer List viewer membership permits viewing items and their locations in list view.
claims.quote: Content Explorer List viewer: Membership in this role group allows you to see each item and its location in list view.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Content Explorer Content viewer membership permits viewing item contents.
claims.quote: Content Explorer Content viewer: Membership in this role group allows you to view the contents of each item in the list.

claims.claim: Content viewer is also required to see item names in list view.
claims.quote: Additionally, this role is also required to view name of items in list view, which might contain sensitive data.

claims.claim: The Compliance administrator Entra ID role grants access to the Content Explorer tab.
claims.quote: To access the content explorer tab, assign an account membership in any one of these Entra ID roles or Purview roles. Entra ID roles: Compliance administrator

claims.claim: The Security administrator Entra ID role grants access to the Content Explorer tab.
claims.quote: Permissions to access the content explorer tab ... Entra ID roles ... Security administrator

claims.claim: The Compliance data administrator Entra ID role grants access to the Content Explorer tab.
claims.quote: Permissions to access the content explorer tab ... Entra ID roles ... Compliance data administrator

claims.claim: The documented Information Protection roles and role groups also grant Content Explorer tab access.
claims.quote: Information Protection Admin; Information Protection Analyst; Information Protection Investigator; Information Protection Reader ... Information Protection; Information Protection Admins; Information Protection Analysts; Information Protection Investigators; Information Protection Readers

claims.claim: Tab-access roles alone do not grant access to item lists or contents.
claims.quote: Membership in these roles doesn't grant permission to view the list of items in content explorer or to view the contents of the items in content explorer.

claims.claim: List viewer and Content viewer permissions are independent and not cumulative, so both are needed to list items and read their contents.
claims.quote: These are independent role groups and aren't cumulative. ... If you want that same account to also be able to view the contents of the items in the list, grant Content Explorer Content viewer rights as well.

claims.claim: Role management role holders can assign Content Explorer role group membership.
claims.quote: Role management role holders in Microsoft Purview can assign the necessary Content Explorer List Viewer, and Content Explorer Content Viewer role group membership.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Content Explorer supports administrative-unit restrictions on its list-viewer and content-viewer permissions.
claims.quote: Content Explorer support administrative units. Members of role groups that have the data classification list viewer or data classification content viewer role ... can be restricted by administrative unit assignments within content explorer.

claims.claim: The permissions page supports security-group membership only in Microsoft 365 commercial cloud organisations.
claims.quote: Security groups are supported only in Microsoft 365 commercial cloud organizations.

claims.claim: The same role-group add-members procedure includes selecting members and choosing Assign admin units.
claims.quote: If the selected users or groups need to be assigned to administrative units, select the users or groups and select Assign admin units.

claims.claim: The data explorer page says encrypted sensitivity labels are not surfaced on content explorer for SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: Encrypted sensitivity labels are not surfaced on content explorer for SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Content Explorer counts can take up to seven days to update.
claims.quote: It can take up to seven days for counts to update in content explorer and 14 days for files that are in SharePoint.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Updates for SharePoint files can take 14 days.
claims.quote: It can take up to seven days for counts to update in content explorer and 14 days for files that are in SharePoint.
